newsitem.title: USA: Charges for Malcolm Shabazz upgraded.
newsitem.headline: Charges for Malcolm Shabazz upgraded.

text.p: Charges against 12-year-old Malcolm Shabazz, accused of setting the fire that killed his grandmother Betty Shabazz, were upgraded by the Westchester County attorney Tuesday though the new charges were not disclosed.
The New York City medical examiner has ruled Betty Shabazz's death was a homicide. It is possible the boy will eventually face murder charges.
The boy, who allegedly set the fire with gasoline in his grandmother's Yonkers, N.Y., apartment last month, has been charged with juvenile delinquency.

At a hearing before Westchester County Family Court Judge Howard Spitz, Malcolm Shabazz's lawyers were given a list of new charges but they will not be made public until Thursday when the boy pleads to them.
Betty Shabazz, 63, widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, died June 23 from burns she suffered in the June 1 fire.
The child's mother Qubilah, the daughter of Malcolm X and Betty Shabazz, was not in court for the hearing.
Lawyers told the judge there was no need to hold a competancy hearing as planned because the boy was able to understand the charges against him.
Outside court, Percy Sutton, one of the boy's lawyers, said the reason they did not dispute his competance was because of the decision by the court to allow the press to cover the proceeding.
Because the boy is younger than 13, the maximum sentence he could get if convicted is 18 months, but he could be kept in a detention facility until he is 18 years old.
Asked whether he would consider a plea deal, Sutton said: "We'll decide that as we go along. We don't want to try the case here."
